themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 4700% surge (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Central Harlem's public spaces.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (4700% spike, z-score: 17.76)
Highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating sudden and dramatic deviation from baseline
No prior Reddit or news coverage suggests this is an emerging, unreported phenomenon
reporting_angles: Ground canvas: Are residents seeing new unauthorized advertisements, political posters, or event promotions appearing overnight across specific neighborhoods?
Enforcement gap: Has the city's illegal posting enforcement operation been paused, scaled back, or redirected away from Central Harlem in the past 2 weeks?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 46 LAST WEEK from a 7.6 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 503% spike (z-score: 5.06)—indicating rapid pavement, pothole, or sidewalk degradation across the district.
evidence: 46 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs 7.6 weekly average (503% increase, z-score: 5.06)
Aligns with CB budget requests for 'New equipment for maintenance' (Department of Parks & Recreation) filed repeatedly, suggesting long-standing infrastructure neglect now accelerating
455 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days (388 alterations), suggesting possible construction activity worsening street conditions
reporting_angles: Mapping the damage: Walk specific blocks in Central Harlem and photograph/document potholes, cracked pavement, and sidewalk buckling. Are certain areas worse than others?
Maintenance readiness: Has DSNY or DEP reduced street repair crews or delayed pothole filling schedules in this district recently?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti & Illegal Posting Convergence
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 8 LAST WEEK from 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 10.61), converging with the illegal posting spike THIS WEEK, suggesting simultaneous deterioration in public space maintenance and possible gang or tag activity.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 10.61)
Convergence with 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK (z-score: 17.76)—two distinct 311 categories spiking simultaneously
Combined signal suggests either coordinated youth activity or systematic enforcement withdrawal across public space maintenance
reporting_angles: Tagger network: Are tags coming from the same artist(s) or crew? Are they claiming territory or protesting something?
Enforcement capacity: Has the city's anti-graffiti task force or Community Board 10's sanitation enforcement been diverted or depleted?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from 0.2 weekly average—a 1900% spike (z-score: 7.18)—raising questions about whether enforcement is ramping up or if illegal vendor activity is escalating in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score: 7.18)
Unclear whether spike reflects aggressive city enforcement or proliferation of unlicensed vendors; requires clarification through 311 complaint text review
Timing overlaps with illegal posting and graffiti spikes, suggesting possible neighborhood destabilization or enforcement policy shift
reporting_angles: Vendor proliferation or enforcement blitz: Are unlicensed vendors (food carts, merchandise) flooding Central Harlem streets, or has NYPD/DOH launched an enforcement operation?
Community impact: Are street vendors viewed as nuisance or as economic engine? Talk to residents and vendors themselves.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Up 63%
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints rose to 125 LAST WEEK from 76.6 weekly average—a 63% increase (z-score: 4.78)—suggesting enforcement slack or increased double-parking/fire hydrant violations in Central Harlem.
evidence: 125 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs 76.6 weekly average (63% increase, z-score: 4.78)
Consistent with street-level enforcement gap hypothesis suggested by graffiti, illegal posting, and vendor enforcement spikes
Illegal parking is lowest-severity of the spikes but part of broader pattern
reporting_angles: Parking enforcement capacity: Have NYPD or DSNY traffic enforcement operations been reduced or redeployed?
Resident frustration: Are parking violations blocking fire hydrants, creating public safety issues, or impeding street cleaning?
